prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: EN · Plan comparison (language en).
Grid: 5 columns × 6 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Feature" · longest unbreakable word 56px · one-line width 83px
  col 2: header "Free" · longest unbreakable word 79px · one-line width 79px
  col 3: header "Pro" · longest unbreakable word 66px · one-line width 66px
  col 4: header "Enterprise" · longest unbreakable word 75px · one-line width 229px
  col 5: header "Notes" · longest unbreakable word 73px · one-line width 419px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 360px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 359px.
This table cannot fit without splitting words at 360px. You MAY choose a total wider than 359px (the reader then scrolls horizontally), or squeeze and accept splits — a design decision.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

The image shows the table's content with every cell on one line, so you can read everything. Study it first.
1) Understand it: what is the table for, how will people read, scan and compare it, which columns play the same or similar role, which values must stay intact, which text may wrap naturally, and where existing row height could absorb wrapping.
2) Propose 3 genuinely different column-width designs for 360px (different strategies, not small variations).
Reply ONLY JSON: {"understanding":{"purpose":"","reading":"","groups":["columns that belong together and why"],"keep_intact":[""],"may_wrap":[""]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[int px per column, column 1 first],"idea":"one sentence"}]}

log.raw: {"understanding":{"purpose":"A feature-by-feature plan comparison: readers check what each tier includes and use Notes for caveats.","reading":"Scan down the Feature column, then move horizontally across Free, Pro and Enterprise to compare the same capability; Notes is consulted only when a value needs explanation.","groups":["Free, Pro and Enterprise are parallel plan-value columns and should read as a comparable set","Feature is the row-label column that anchors each comparison","Notes is a secondary annotation column, not a fourth plan"],"keep_intact":["the headers Feature, Free, Pro, Enterprise, Notes","short values such as 3, 2 GB, 100 GB, 30 days, 1 year, Custom and Email","Community and Unlimited where the chosen width permits","SSO / SAML as a single label"],"may_wrap":["Notes prose","24/7 phone & dedicated at its spaces","SSO / SAML at the slash if the Feature column is tight","long plan values at word boundaries when space is squeezed"]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[82,78,64,80,55],"idea":"No-scroll compromise: keep every column visible, give Feature and Enterprise slightly more room, and accept word splits plus a very narrow Notes column."},{"name":"B","widths":[90,100,90,110,180],"idea":"Plan-first horizontal scroll: fund Free, Pro and Enterprise so their headers and characteristic values stay intact, while Notes wraps at a readable measure."},{"name":"C","widths":[84,92,82,102,240],"idea":"Notes-readable horizontal scroll: give the long annotation column a wide measure to keep rows shallow, accepting tighter plan columns and some splitting in Community/Unlimited."}]}
